label: input z at original positions 2-3
explanation: Fires only when the input token is z during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. Activation is strong (about 0.6-0.9) only at t = 2 or 3; z at t = 1 or t = 4 gives just a weak trace (around 0.05 of max), and z at t = 0 or t >= 5 gives nothing. This rule has dev precision 1.0, recall 0.90 and mass recall 0.99; every missed activation is one of those weak t = 1/4 traces. It does not fire on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (only 23 tiny activations there). The strongest examples are z at t = 3 after letter prefixes; in the low-quartile examples a digit comes earlier in the sequence, but that pattern was only seen in examples and not scored.

issues: Minor wording problem, not a refutation. Dev split: z at t=1 is active on 2137 of about 19.7k steps, and z at t=4 on 1408. On test, the t=1 predicate has precision 0.135 and mass recall 0.005, and the t=4 predicate has precision 0.10 and mass recall 0.004. So at t=1 and t=4 a z usually gives no activation at all. When it does fire, the activation is weak (0.04-0.09 of max). The 'weak trace' wording should say these traces are occasional.
Widening the predicate to t=1..4 recovers recall (0.999) but drops precision to 0.58. Test F1 falls from 0.949 to 0.736, so the original narrower predicate is the better one.

The other claims hold. On test the predicate has precision 1.0, recall 0.903, F1 0.949 and mass recall 0.991. It never fires on any token other than z, never fires on <DEL>, and fires on only 23 copy-phase steps out of 2.7M (dev). Test misses cover 0.9% of activation mass, and all the samples shown were z at t=1 or t=4 with values of 0.04-0.09. There were no test false positives.
The digit-earlier-in-prefix magnitude pattern is unscored, but the explanation already says so.
